sections.h2: Tenant rights when a Maine landlord wants to sell
sections.html:
A sale does not cancel a tenant's rights. The tenant keeps the protections that come with the tenancy, and the landlord still has to follow the same notice, deposit and court rules. The basics: a safe and habitable home, written notice of rent increases, reasonable notice before entry, a deposit returned on time, and no eviction without a court order.

Two kinds of rental matter most. A tenant with a written lease holds a fixed term, and the lease controls the notice rules. A tenant with no lease, or with a lease silent on notice, is a tenant at will and can be asked to leave on written notice under 14 M.R.S. §6002. Work out which kind of tenancy you have before you list a rental or accept an offer.

sections.h2: Can a landlord evict because the house is being sold?
sections.html:
Not on the landlord's say-so. A landlord must go to court to remove a tenant, and self-help such as changing locks, blocking entry or shutting off utilities is illegal. The first step is a notice to quit, which is not a court order and does not by itself require the tenant to leave.

For a tenant at will, either side can end the tenancy with at least 30 days' written notice. If rent has been paid through a date later than the end of the 30 days, the notice must expire on or after that date. The notice has to advise the tenant of the right to contest the termination in court, and the landlord must attach the Judicial Branch's form notice to any notice terminating a tenancy (14 M.R.S. §6001, subsection 7).

If the tenant has an unexpired lease, the lease term governs, and if a lease expired less than 7 days ago, no notice is required. A buyer who wants the house vacant should price that wait into the deal.

sections.h2: What a buyer takes with a rented house
sections.html:
A third-party buyer cannot start an eviction case against a tenant at will unless the tenant received proper §6002 notice from the grantor or the grantee. That limit is in §6001, subsection 2, and it is the rule most relevant to a sale.

Put simply, a change of owner does not let anyone skip the notice step. Either the seller serves a proper notice before closing, or the buyer serves one after. If a foreclosure is pending or a judgment has been entered, a bona fide tenancy may end only under the federal Protecting Tenants at Foreclosure Act of 2009 (§6001, subsection 1-A).

  • Sellers who want a vacant house should serve notice early and keep proof of service.
  • Buyers who will keep the tenant should ask for the lease, the rent history and the deposit amount.
  • A cash buyer who accepts the tenant as is can close without waiting for the unit to empty.

Settle in writing, in the purchase agreement, how the security deposit passes at closing, and have an attorney review it.

A deposit cannot exceed two months' rent, and the landlord must hold it in a separate account during the tenancy (§6032).

After the tenancy ends, §6033 requires the landlord to return the full deposit, or return the balance with an itemized written statement, within the period in a written agreement (not more than 30 days) or within 21 days for a tenancy at will. Deductions can cover unpaid rent, damage and storage or disposal of left-behind property, but not normal wear and tear.

RuleMaine standard
Deposit cap (14 M.R.S. §6032)Two months' rent
Return deadline, written agreement (§6033)As stated, up to 30 days
Return deadline, tenancy at will (§6033)21 days
Missed deadline (§6033)Landlord loses the right to withhold any part
Wrongful retention (§6034)Twice the amount, plus fees, after 7 days' notice

In a lawsuit under §6034 the landlord must prove that withholding was not wrongful, so clean records matter when a rental changes hands.

Tenants at will must receive 75 days' written notice for increases over 10% and 45 days' notice for smaller ones. The rule covers all rental housing, including rented mobile homes, tenants cannot waive it, and increases within 12 months add together toward the 10% line.

A tenant with an unexpired lease cannot have rent raised above the lease amount. Mobile home parks have their own law requiring 90 days' notice for all rent and fee increases. A tenant charged without proper notice may recover rent, interest and reasonable attorney's fees, and can complain to the Attorney General's office.

A new owner who wants to raise rent runs the same notice clock. A buyer underwriting a rental should assume the first increase takes at least 45 days to take effect.

sections.h2: Showing the house to a buyer
sections.html:
Yes, a landlord can enter with reasonable notice. Twenty-four hours is presumed reasonable, entry must happen at reasonable times, and a tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry for showings to prospective buyers, lenders, tenants or contractors.

  • Give written notice for each showing, and keep a copy.
  • Group showings on fewer days to avoid a harassment complaint.
  • Emergencies are the exception to the notice rule.

Retaliation is the risk. Under §6001 retaliation is presumed, subject to rebuttal, when the tenant engaged in protected activity such as a habitability complaint within 6 months before the landlord's action, and no writ of possession may issue unless that presumption is rebutted.

sections.h2: Repairs and habitability before a sale
sections.html:
All rented housing must be fit for human habitation, and an unrepaired problem can follow the property into a sale dispute. A tenant can sue for repairs only after showing that the condition endangers health or safety, the tenant did not cause it, written notice was given, the tenant was current on rent, and the landlord failed to fix it in a reasonable time.

Repair and deduct is available when the repair costs less than $500 or half the monthly rent, whichever is greater. The tenant gives written notice, and if the landlord does not act within 14 days (or promptly in an emergency) the tenant may arrange the repair and deduct the reasonable cost. A landlord who supplies heat must keep the system able to maintain 68 degrees Fahrenheit when it is 20 degrees below zero outside. Bedbug reports require an inspection within 5 days and a pest control contact within 10 days.

Under §6002, subsection 3, a tenant sued for nonpayment can raise an unrepaired habitability violation the landlord knew about, and a court that finds the unit unfit can reduce the rent owed to fair rental value.

sections.h2: If a tenant will not leave
sections.html:
The landlord files a Forcible Entry and Detainer action after the notice to quit expires. §6004 requires a plain-language form notice to be attached to the summons and complaint for residential tenants. The usual sequence:

  1. Notice to quit: 7 days for nonpayment when rent is 7 or more days late, or 30 days for a no-cause tenancy at will.
  2. Court forms: complaint, summons and information sheet, with a $100 filing fee and $5 per summons.
  3. Service: by the sheriff, at least 14 days before the hearing.
  4. Hearing: mediation is available at the court on the hearing day.
  5. Writ of possession: can issue 7 days after judgment, and the tenant has 48 hours after service.

A nonpayment tenant who pays all rent due plus fees before the writ issues keeps the tenancy. Back rent is a separate case, often in Small Claims Court. The notice, service and writ periods alone add up to several weeks, so a buyer who needs the house empty should expect to wait.

sections.h2: Should you consider a cash sale?
sections.html: Owners with a tenant who will not leave, a lease that runs past the planned closing, or a deposit dispute may find a traditional sale hard to time around occupancy and condition. Cash Home Buyers buys Maine houses as-is, and you can ask us about a house with a tenant in it. We do not quote a price until we have seen the property and the lease. Our Maine property tax guide and probate guide cover other issues that often come with a rental sale.

faqs.q: How much notice does a Maine landlord need to give to end a tenancy at will?
faqs.a: At least 30 days' written notice under 14 M.R.S. §6002, or 7 days for stated causes such as rent 7 or more days late. The notice must say the tenant may contest it in court.

faqs.q: Does a lease end when the landlord sells the property?
faqs.a: A sale alone does not end a lease, and the buyer steps into the landlord's place. A third-party buyer cannot evict a tenant at will unless the tenant received proper §6002 notice from the seller or the buyer.

faqs.q: How much can a landlord charge for a security deposit in Maine?
faqs.a: No more than two months' rent. The landlord must return it or send an itemized statement within 30 days under a written agreement, or within 21 days for a tenancy at will.

faqs.q: How much notice is required for a rent increase?
faqs.a: 75 days' written notice for increases over 10% and 45 days for smaller increases for tenants at will. Mobile home parks require 90 days.

faqs.q: Can a tenant refuse to let a buyer see the home?
faqs.a: Not unreasonably. A tenant may not unreasonably refuse entry for showings to prospective buyers, and 24 hours' notice is presumed reasonable. Landlords cannot shut off utilities or change the locks to force the issue, because self-help evictions are illegal in Maine.
